entities.summary:
Ulrich of Zell, also known as Wulderic, sometimes of Cluny or of Regensburg, was a Cluniac reformer of Germany, abbot, founder and saint.

    Born around 1025 in the Holy Roman Empire, Ulrich was a member of the powerful Cluniac Order, a reform movement that aimed to revive the spiritual practices of the early Christian Church. He played a crucial role in the reformation of the Cluniac Order in Germany and was instrumental in the establishment of the monastery of Zell, near Regensburg, which became a major center of learning and spirituality.

    Ulrich's commitment to the Cluniac ideals of reform and renewal was shaped by his experiences as a monk and his encounters with the Holy Roman Emperor, Henry III. He was particularly drawn to the teachings of Gregory the Great and the writings of the Cluniac master, Aelred of Rievaulx.

    Ulrich's legacy extends beyond his own monastery, as he helped to spread the Cluniac ideals throughout Germany and beyond. He was a key figure in the development of the medieval reform movement, which sought to revitalize the spiritual practices of the Church.

    Despite his significant influence, Ulrich's life and legacy are not well documented in modern scholarship, and much remains to be discovered about his life and work.
